current_price_note: current_price is quoted in GBp (LSE secondary listing, WISE.L) per dashboard convention. Primary listing is Nasdaq (WSE), which closed at $11.93 on 31-Jul-2026; cross-checked here via live GBPUSD spot: 885.6p x 1.3487 / 100 = $11.944, consistent with WSE within rounding/timing.
horizon_rationale: 10-year explicit build used because the component-built owner-FCF margin is still climbing at year 5 in all three scenarios (base 19.3% at Y5 vs 22.9% at Y10; bull 21.8% vs 26.3%; bear 16.4% vs 18.5%) -- capitalizing an immature Y5 margin via Gordon growth would understate intrinsic value. Wise's own FY2026 investment-year margin reset (adj-EBITDA-incl-SBC margin fell to 28.0% from 38.7% in FY2025) means the business needs several years to both recover from the reinvestment trough AND grow into the new structurally larger compliance/servicing cost base (Servicing+G&A ~30-31% of net revenue, per management commentary) before settling into a mature margin.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: Point-in-time fully diluted ~1,000-1,005m per WISE.L_CoreFloat_Inputs.md (midpoint 1,002.5m used), NOT the 1,029.7m FY2026 backward-looking weighted-average diluted share count. Class B supervoting shares (208.9m, no economic interest) excluded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt is NEGATIVE $1,873.7m (i.e. net CORPORATE cash of +$1,873.7m ex-leases), per WISE.L_CoreFloat_Inputs.md Section 2 -- reconciled from the 20-F balance sheet (cash, AFS debt securities, processor/customer receivables LESS customer balances/money-transmission liabilities/processor payables LESS EMTN carrying value and accrued interest). This explicitly EXCLUDES the ~$29.96bn of customer safeguarded funds and ~$4.58bn of AFS securities backing customer balances, which are not available to equity holders. The $550-750m of this cash that is trapped as regulatory capital in licensed subsidiaries is NOT deducted here (per task instruction to 'use that' net-cash figure) -- a reader wanting the freely-distributable-only view should use ~$1.10-1.30bn instead of $1.87bn.
inputs.interest_income_note: This is CORPORATE interest income on Wise's own (non-customer) cash/investments ($63.0m FY2026, per WISE.L.duckdb kpis table InterestIncomeCorporate) -- NOT the $609.2m of NET interest income on CUSTOMER balances, which is a genuine, recurring, scaling operating revenue line (~24% of group net revenue) and is correctly left inside net revenue/EBITDA. Corporate interest income is stripped from FCF because net corporate cash ($1,873.7m) is ~3.9x the owner-FCF base ($479.0m), i.e. well above the 1x materiality threshold -- leaving it in would double-count the cash pile (once as interest income in FCF, once as net cash added to enterprise value).
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/20-F cash-flow-statement add-back (FY2026 20-F Note 19, USD-restated for FY2024-26: $95.5m/$74.6m/$91.1m). FY2022 ($42.2m GBP) and FY2023 ($58.2m GBP) converted to USD at average FY exchange rates (1.36 and 1.19 respectively, back-solved from the Metrics.csv net-revenue/GBP-revenue ratio) to $57.4m and $69.3m. No separate net-share-settlement equity-award-tax cash outflow is disclosed anywhere in the financing activities section or Note 19 -- Wise's employee awards are structured as near-nil-strike options (weighted-average exercise price $0.10-0.11) exercised for cash consideration, not RSUs settled net-of-tax-withholding, so the cash-flow-statement SBC add-back is the complete, undiscounted cost (no equity-award-tax add-on needed, unlike DUOL).
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2026 'Repurchases of shares' financing-activity cash outflow (20-F cash flow statement), the company's largest buyback year to date and the base for the newly launched up-to-$540m/GBP405m program (through 31-Mar-2027).
inputs.annual_share_growth_note: Buyback cash ($473.4m FY2026) is ~5x SBC ($95.5m), so uncovered_dilution = max(0, 95.5 - 473.4) = 0. Share count held flat at 1,002.5m across the projection horizon -- consistent with 'buyback-heavy names' in the SBC-adjustment framework (Wise now behaves like AAPL/V on this dimension, not like DUOL).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (41.0%) diverges sharply from net revenue 3yr CAGR (29.7%) because equity is inflated by retained earnings compounding off a small FY2022 base and by FX translation gains booked to OCI (e.g. +$67.7m FY2026), not because the underlying business is compounding book value at 41%/yr -- per the ticker-specific mandate, net revenue CAGR (not equity CAGR) is used as the primary growth driver precisely because of this distortion (here from retained-earnings/FX effects rather than buybacks, which is the more common Wise distortion). EPS 3yr CAGR (54.9%) also diverges from revenue growth, reflecting operating leverage off a near-breakeven FY2022 base -- not used as primary driver. Reported FCF CAGR (35.9%) is NOT reliable either: it is inflated by FY2025's outsized 31.8% owner-FCF margin (a working-capital/tax-timing high-water mark) and depressed by FY2026's deliberate heavy-investment year (19.1% owner-FCF margin) -- the owner-FCF series swings between 12.8% (FY2022) and 31.8% (FY2025) margin on net revenue with no clean trend, which is exactly why Step 1c mandates a component build (EBITDA-SBC-D&A-tax-capex-WC) rather than extrapolating any single historical FCF growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF 3yr CAGR (38.3%) is actually ABOVE the reported FCF 3yr CAGR (35.9%) for Wise, the opposite of the usual SBC-dilution pattern -- this is because Wise's SBC is a small (~3.8-7.6%) and DECLINING share of net revenue (nil-cost/near-nil-strike option plan, not a Silicon-Valley-style RSU program), and FY2026's step-up in SBC ($95.5m from $74.6m) coincided with a reported-FCF dip, so the SBC deduction understates FY2026 relative to FY2025 by a similar proportion as reported FCF understates it. This is a genuinely different SBC profile than DUOL/US tech peers: Wise's buybacks ($473.4m FY2026) already run ~5x SBC ($95.5m), so uncovered dilution is zero and the share-count mechanism (not the FCF-deduction mechanism) is where SBC would normally bite -- it doesn't, because Wise over-covers it via buybacks.

base.wc_capture_note: NEGATIVE capture: unlike subscription businesses where deferred revenue provides a working-capital TAILWIND on growth, Wise's net working-capital items (accounts receivable, prepaid compliance/insurance/tech costs, accounts payable/tax timing) have been a consistent net DRAG in every historical year (-$124m FY2024, -$78m FY2025, -$157m FY2026, ex customer-float movements which are already excluded from FCF). Modeled as -12% of the YoY revenue increase (base case), i.e. working capital consumes cash as the business grows, not releases it.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: FY2026 cash tax rate was 24.6% of IBT ($162.5m/$660.4m), FY2025 was 25.7% -- both already close to the UK statutory rate (25%) and a blended multi-jurisdictional rate; no valuation-allowance-release or one-off credit is evident (unlike DUOL), so held flat at 26% rather than ramped from an abnormal starting point.

wacc_rationale.starting_point: ~9.0% unlevered cost of equity baseline for a large-cap, profitable, net-cash global fintech (CAPM-style: risk-free ~4.3% US10Y/UK gilt blend + equity risk premium ~5%, low beta offset by growth-stock volatility)

regulatory_risk_premium_components.component: OCC national trust bank charter denial (23-24 Jul 2026)
regulatory_risk_premium_components.rationale: Explicit AML-adequacy denial (not a scope/technicality issue), Wise the outlier among fintech OCC charter applicants (8 of 11 approved since 2020); delays direct Fed rail access and US cost-reduction optionality to H2 2028 at the earliest

regulatory_risk_premium_components.component: Belgian criminal AML investigation (Wise Europe SA)
regulatory_risk_premium_components.rationale: Unprovisioned, unquantified criminal (not administrative) process against the entity holding Wise's sole EEA passporting licence, underpinning ~27% of group net revenue; prosecutors reportedly finalizing a direct summons to criminal court with NBB referral expected; drew the single sharpest stock reaction of 2026 (-20% intraday) and is a genuine licence-level tail risk, not merely a fine

regulatory_risk_premium_components.component: Multi-state Consent Order tail (through Jul-2027) + pattern of repeat AML findings across 3 jurisdictions in ~12 months
regulatory_risk_premium_components.rationale: Independent third-party validation and SAR lookback obligations continue through mid-2027 and gate any US charter refiling; the recurrence of the same root-cause finding (inadequate customer/transaction due diligence) across US state, US federal, and Belgian regulators reads as systemic rather than isolated

wacc_rationale.governance_rationale: CEO's Class B supervoting shares extended a further decade (to 2036) despite co-founder opposition; ~50% voting control on ~18% economic interest is a persistent overhang the OCC's letter arguably also touches on (questioning management/board depth)
wacc_rationale.final_wacc_build: ~9.0% base + 2.0% stacked regulatory premium + 0.25% governance premium + a small residual for competitive/rate-cycle risk = 11.5% base case WACC. Bull case (10.5%) assumes the Belgian and US regulatory matters resolve without licence-level consequence; bear case (13.0%) assumes the regulatory premium proves understated (e.g. an adverse Belgian criminal finding or NBB action).

sbc_noncash_memo.description: Memo value: what the business would be worth if SBC were treated as a non-cash accounting item with no economic cost to shareholders (i.e. added back to FCF with no share-count consequence) -- the honest measure of how much of the valuation depends on SBC treatment.
sbc_noncash_memo.note: The spread is modest (~13% of base IV) relative to peers like DUOL because Wise's SBC is small (~3.8% of net revenue, declining) and already more than fully offset by buybacks (uncovered_dilution = 0) -- Wise is a buyback-heavy name on this dimension, not a dilution-heavy one.

entry_price.methodology: Entry price = (PV of Yr1-10 owner FCF discounted at 15% hurdle + PV of Year-10 terminal value [min of Gordon-at-WACC and 20x cap, per Step 4] discounted at 15% - net_debt) / projected_shares[10]. Full FCF path discounted at the 15% hurdle throughout, per the 2026-07-21 entry-price fix -- terminal value is computed with WACC (the fair price a future buyer pays) but discounted back to today at 15% (the buyer's required return).

sensitivity.note: Matrix is base-case intrinsic value per share (USD) across WACC (rows) and terminal growth (columns); base-case growth path, margin build and shares held constant. WACC range centered on 11.5% base (+/-2pp); terminal growth centered on 3.0% base (+/-1pp).

sanity_check.method: Fetched 10y monthly WISE.L (LSE, GBp) prices via Yahoo Finance, matched March FY-end closes to FY rows, converted to USD at each FY's average GBPUSD spot, and computed historical P/E, P/S, P/B and EV/owner-FCF on an SBC-adjusted basis. FY2022-FY2023 excluded as hypergrowth-era outliers (P/E 52-120x off a near-breakeven earnings base). FY2024-26 is the anchor period.

FY2022.note: excluded as hypergrowth-era outlier (near-breakeven EPS base)

trip_conditions_checked.threshold: 24.5x (hist P/E avg) x 2 = 49.0x; base implied P/FCF-per-share ~28.3x and bull ~38.9x are both below this
trip_conditions_checked.detail: Base case upside is 13.0%, not >100%, so this condition is not triggered
trip_conditions_checked.exit_multiple_detail: Current trailing EV/owner-FCF is 21.1x. Base implied exit multiple is 12.1x and bull is 14.8x -- both below current, meaning the DCF assumes de-rating/normalization toward a lower steady-state multiple as growth decelerates, not multiple expansion.

sanity_check.result: PASS. No fixes required. Base-case implied multiples sit below the FY24-26 ex-outlier historical average and well below the current trailing multiple, i.e. the DCF does not assume any multiple expansion -- consistent with a decelerating-growth fintech normalizing off a temporarily depressed FY2026 margin, with an explicit regulatory risk premium in WACC reflecting the OCC denial and Belgian AML probe. Bull case (76% upside) is notable but does not breach the >100%-upside trip threshold, and its exit multiple (14.8x) remains below today's trailing 21.1x.

risk_disclosures.belgian_aml_investigation: Unprovisioned, unquantified criminal investigation into Wise Europe SA (~27% of group net revenue via its EEA passporting licence). Not separately modeled as a discrete scenario haircut in this DCF -- instead reflected via a +100bp WACC premium (of the 200bp total regulatory premium) in all three scenarios. A reader wanting an explicit Scenario-D-style forced-restructuring/fine haircut should consult WISE.L_CoreFloat_Inputs.md Section 5/8, which bounds the EU own-funds requirement at only ~EUR13-18m (small) but flags the licence itself, not the capital requirement, as the real tail risk.
risk_disclosures.occ_charter_denial: Reflected via a +50bp WACC premium; does not affect existing 48-state US money-transmitter operations, but delays the GENIUS Act stablecoin charter refiling path to a realistic H2 2027 filing / H2 2028 approval at the earliest.
risk_disclosures.net_cash_usage_note: This DCF uses the full $1,873.7m net corporate cash figure per task instruction, NOT the $1.10-1.30bn distributable-only figure that nets out $550-750m of regulatory capital trapped in licensed subsidiaries. A reader modeling a return-of-capital or wind-down scenario should substitute the lower, distributable figure.

valuation_philosophy: Wise is modeled as a decelerating high-growth fintech using a 10-year component-built owner-FCF model, not a flat-margin extrapolation of the FY2026 heavy-investment year. Net revenue CAGR (29.7% trailing 3yr) is the growth driver, not equity CAGR (41.0%, inflated by retained-earnings/FX-translation compounding) or reported FCF (which swings 12.8%-31.8% margin on net revenue with no clean trend due to working-capital/tax timing). Owner FCF is built bottom-up each year: adjusted EBITDA margin ramps from the FY2026 trough (28.5%, post the deliberate compliance/tech/marketing reinvestment step-up) toward a mature 36% (base case) -- materially below the pre-reset FY2024/25 peak of ~42.5%/38.7%, honoring the mandate that Servicing+G&A opex near 30-31% of net revenue is now a permanent structural floor, not a temporary spike. SBC is deducted at its actual (small, ~3.8% of revenue, declining) level -- Wise's near-nil-strike option program plus a buyback ($473.4m FY2026) running ~5x SBC means uncovered dilution is zero and the share count stays flat, the opposite dynamic to DUOL. Working capital is modeled as a net DRAG scaling with revenue growth (not a subscription-style deferred-revenue tailwind), matching Wise's actual multi-year pattern. Net corporate cash (+$1,873.7m, replacing a near-zero net-debt assumption in the prior model) is added to enterprise value, with the offsetting corporate interest income ($63.0m) stripped from FCF to avoid double-counting. WACC (11.5% base) explicitly stacks a 200bp regulatory risk premium across the OCC charter denial, the Belgian criminal AML investigation into Wise Europe SA, and the pattern of repeat AML findings across three jurisdictions in twelve months, plus a 25bp governance premium for the CEO's extended supervoting control -- on top of a ~9.0% base cost of capital for a large, profitable, net-cash global payments platform. The historical-multiple sanity check passes without requiring any fix: base-case implied multiples sit below Wise's own FY2024-26 trading range and assume no multiple expansion (implied exit multiples of 9.3-14.8x vs today's trailing 21.1x EV/owner-FCF).
